excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >
Nikola Lazarov, CEO and co-founder, contends that this pace and depth would be impossible to replicate without the infrastructure it has built.

Its proprietary technology, built in-house over three years, combines AI infrastructure with experienced M&A advisors who oversee AI-generated work, manage transaction processes, and coordinate communication between both sides.

Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement. First is preparation. It identifies a broad universe of potential buyers — often larger in SMB deals, where smaller companies attract a wider range of acquirers. “We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > > Next is outreach. While the company utilises its existing relationships, it also deploys highly personalised outreach to new buyers. It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals. This enables it to send highly tailored messages at scale, resulting in higher response rates.

“We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers.
It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals.

Eilla AI’s models are probabilistic, and the system does not rely on generic model outputs or training data alone. Instead, it works with structured context provided by the client, combined with data extracted from proprietary databases and licensed external sources — including a dataset built from tens of millions of scraped pages covering around nine million companies.

Eilla AI’s cost structure is fundamentally different. Because AI handles the volume-intensive work, buyer sourcing, outreach and document creation, the firm operates on a success-fee-only basis with no retainers.
> “In our segment, average deal sizes are around €10–20 million, and we charge about a 5 per cent success fee. So a single deal might generate around €500,000.” > >
Eilla AI’s customer is typically the founder or owner of an SMB business looking to sell.

According to Petrov, two things became clear. First, the M&A industry is quite behind in terms of AI adoption — “even large boutiques were only just integrating tools like ChatGPT internally,” he shared. Second, the SMB segment is underserved. The team decided to combine the AI it has built with the expertise of experienced advisors.

Eilla AI has completed Europe’s first M&A deal executed by an AI-native advisory firm, advising on the acquisition of two Central and Eastern European digital marketing agencies, CreateX and Native Digital, by Swedish listed company [White Pearl Technology Group](https://whitepearltech.com/) .

What “AI-native advisory” means in practice Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement.

The founders of both acquired companies credited Eilla AI with making the transactions possible. “Honestly, without Eilla, this deal would not have happened,” said Aleksandar, founder and CEO of CreateX. The reaction from Native Digital was similar.

Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > >

Eilla AI is already seeing early traction in both deal speed and buyer reach. One recent transaction moved from outreach to non-binding offers in around 15 days, with the full process completing within a few months — despite involving multiple companies, shareholders, and a non-obvious buyer. According to Petrov: > “It was a complex deal — multiple companies, multiple shareholders, and a buyer that wouldn’t normally be identified through traditional relationships.” > > Rather than relying on existing networks, the firm identified the buyer through pattern matching at speed against previous acquisitions, surfacing a publicly listed Swedish company that would likely have been missed in a traditional process.

Across its processes so far, Eilla AI reports that around 80 per cent of companies reach the stage of presenting to buyers, suggesting a higher level of early-stage engagement. “In one case, a company that previously secured one NDA with a traditional advisor reached nine NDAs using our process.”

Eilla AI launched its advisory practice at the end of last year and now has around 20 active mandates, with a fee pipeline of approximately €20 million — up more than 15-fold from roughly €1.6 million at the start of the year.

excerpts: We are excited to announce Fuel Ventures’ investment into Eilla AI as part of a $1,500,000 seed round, led by Eleven Ventures. [**Eilla AI**](https://eilla.ai/) is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to power the M&A, VC and PE deal workflow by automating mundane tasks and supporting complex decision making.
**What is Eilla AI?**
Eilla AI's technology automates these processes by mirroring industry professionals using generative AI.

The platform also unlocks new insights and supports complex decision-making through aggregation and analysis of large amounts of information from various sources in significantly less time than is currently possible.

This funding will be vital as we aim to expand our technical team and product offering, while also positioning the business for growth across the M&A, venture capital, and private equity markets.” **Nikola Lazarov, CEO at Eilla AI.**

excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >
Nikola Lazarov, CEO and co-founder, contends that this pace and depth would be impossible to replicate without the infrastructure it has built.

Its proprietary technology, built in-house over three years, combines AI infrastructure with experienced M&A advisors who oversee AI-generated work, manage transaction processes, and coordinate communication between both sides.

Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement. First is preparation. It identifies a broad universe of potential buyers — often larger in SMB deals, where smaller companies attract a wider range of acquirers. “We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > > Next is outreach. While the company utilises its existing relationships, it also deploys highly personalised outreach to new buyers. It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals. This enables it to send highly tailored messages at scale, resulting in higher response rates.

It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals.

Eilla AI’s models are probabilistic, and the system does not rely on generic model outputs or training data alone. Instead, it works with structured context provided by the client, combined with data extracted from proprietary databases and licensed external sources — including a dataset built from tens of millions of scraped pages covering around nine million companies.

Eilla AI’s cost structure is fundamentally different. Because AI handles the volume-intensive work, buyer sourcing, outreach and document creation, the firm operates on a success-fee-only basis with no retainers.
> “In our segment, average deal sizes are around €10–20 million, and we charge about a 5 per cent success fee. So a single deal might generate around €500,000.” > >

According to Petrov, two things became clear. First, the M&A industry is quite behind in terms of AI adoption — “even large boutiques were only just integrating tools like ChatGPT internally,” he shared. Second, the SMB segment is underserved. The team decided to combine the AI it has built with the expertise of experienced advisors.

Eilla AI has completed Europe’s first M&A deal executed by an AI-native advisory firm, advising on the acquisition of two Central and Eastern European digital marketing agencies, CreateX and Native Digital, by Swedish listed company [White Pearl Technology Group](https://whitepearltech.com/) .

The founders of both acquired companies credited Eilla AI with making the transactions possible. “Honestly, without Eilla, this deal would not have happened,” said Aleksandar, founder and CEO of CreateX. The reaction from Native Digital was similar.

Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > >

Eilla AI is already seeing early traction in both deal speed and buyer reach. One recent transaction moved from outreach to non-binding offers in around 15 days, with the full process completing within a few months — despite involving multiple companies, shareholders, and a non-obvious buyer. According to Petrov: > “It was a complex deal — multiple companies, multiple shareholders, and a buyer that wouldn’t normally be identified through traditional relationships.” > > Rather than relying on existing networks, the firm identified the buyer through pattern matching at speed against previous acquisitions, surfacing a publicly listed Swedish company that would likely have been missed in a traditional process.

excerpts: We are excited to announce Fuel Ventures’ investment into Eilla AI as part of a $1,500,000 seed round, led by Eleven Ventures. [**Eilla AI**](https://eilla.ai/) is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to power the M&A, VC and PE deal workflow by automating mundane tasks and supporting complex decision making.
**What is Eilla AI?**
Eilla AI's technology automates these processes by mirroring industry professionals using generative AI.

The platform also unlocks new insights and supports complex decision-making through aggregation and analysis of large amounts of information from various sources in significantly less time than is currently possible.

This funding will be vital as we aim to expand our technical team and product offering, while also positioning the business for growth across the M&A, venture capital, and private equity markets.” **Nikola Lazarov, CEO at Eilla AI.**

We are excited to be leading Eilla AI’s seed funding round and work with its talented team, which uniquely combines deep AI expertise with M&A domain knowledge.”_ **_Eleven Ventures General Partner, Svetozar Georgiev_** _._
A huge congratulations to founders Nikola Lazarov, Nikolay Babulkov and Petar Petrov - we can’t wait to build something great together.

CEO Nikola Lazarov: An AI engineer, former Hedge Fund quant, experience as an early employee at a YC backed startup and a Masters in Generative AI from the University of Cambridge CTO Nikolay Babulkov: An AI engineer with 7 years experience across ML, software and DevOps and papers published at NLP conferences (ACL and CLEF) CCO Petar Petrov: Experience across sales and marketing at high growth startups, including being the Growth Lead at B2B SaaS company Vita Mojo, helping them land a $30m Series B from Battery Ventures.

To date, Eilla AI has been used by advisors and investors from more than 50 M&A banks and VC and PE funds to help optimise specific tasks by researching, aggregating, and analysing information from key industry sources and internal data.
We tackle this problem by analysing all of the essential information and then providing a report in the appropriate format for our clients.

We are excited to announce Fuel Ventures’ investment into Eilla AI as part of a $1,500,000 seed round, led by Eleven Ventures. [**Eilla AI**](https://eilla.ai/) is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to power the M&A, VC and PE deal workflow by automating mundane tasks and supporting complex decision making. A huge congratulations to founders Nikola Lazarov, Nikolay Babulkov and Petar Petrov - we can’t wait to build something great together.

A British generative AI startup has raised $1.5m (£1.2m) in seed funding to provide automation tools that assist investment firms with deal flow. London-based Eilla AI says its platform “mirrors” industry professionals to carry out tasks such as market mapping, document creation and offer comparisons. “The bottom line is that financial professionals are paid to think, not waste time on mundane tasks,” said Nikola Lazarov, CEO of Eilla AI. “But the amount of time and effort it takes a junior at a financial firm to map out the companies in a specific industry, for example, can spiral quickly.” Eleven Ventures led the seed round, with Fuel Ventures and its founder Mark Pearson (as an angel investor) also taking part. The startup plans to use the seed capital to grow into Europe and America. Eilla AI says over 50 M&A banks, VCs and PE funds have used its financial generative AI software. Svetozar Georgiev, general partner at Eleven Ventures, said: “The daily work of M&A, VC and PE professionals hasn’t evolved much in the past 30 years, dominated by lots of manual data retrieval and analysis, as well as mundane document creation.” Georgiev added that Eilla’s generative AI platform will “provide superhuman productivity” and complete tasks in minutes rather than hours or days.
Eleven Ventures led the seed round, with Fuel Ventures and its founder Mark Pearson (as an angel investor) also taking part.
The startup plans to use the seed capital to grow into Europe and America.

excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >
Nikola Lazarov, CEO and co-founder, contends that this pace and depth would be impossible to replicate without the infrastructure it has built.

Its proprietary technology, built in-house over three years, combines AI infrastructure with experienced M&A advisors who oversee AI-generated work, manage transaction processes, and coordinate communication between both sides.

Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement. First is preparation. It identifies a broad universe of potential buyers — often larger in SMB deals, where smaller companies attract a wider range of acquirers. “We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > > Next is outreach. While the company utilises its existing relationships, it also deploys highly personalised outreach to new buyers. It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals. This enables it to send highly tailored messages at scale, resulting in higher response rates.

“We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers.
It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals.

Eilla AI’s models are probabilistic, and the system does not rely on generic model outputs or training data alone. Instead, it works with structured context provided by the client, combined with data extracted from proprietary databases and licensed external sources — including a dataset built from tens of millions of scraped pages covering around nine million companies.

Eilla AI’s cost structure is fundamentally different. Because AI handles the volume-intensive work, buyer sourcing, outreach and document creation, the firm operates on a success-fee-only basis with no retainers.
> “In our segment, average deal sizes are around €10–20 million, and we charge about a 5 per cent success fee. So a single deal might generate around €500,000.” > >
Eilla AI’s customer is typically the founder or owner of an SMB business looking to sell.

According to Petrov, two things became clear. First, the M&A industry is quite behind in terms of AI adoption — “even large boutiques were only just integrating tools like ChatGPT internally,” he shared. Second, the SMB segment is underserved. The team decided to combine the AI it has built with the expertise of experienced advisors.

Eilla AI has completed Europe’s first M&A deal executed by an AI-native advisory firm, advising on the acquisition of two Central and Eastern European digital marketing agencies, CreateX and Native Digital, by Swedish listed company [White Pearl Technology Group](https://whitepearltech.com/) .

What “AI-native advisory” means in practice Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement.

The founders of both acquired companies credited Eilla AI with making the transactions possible. “Honestly, without Eilla, this deal would not have happened,” said Aleksandar, founder and CEO of CreateX. The reaction from Native Digital was similar.

Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > >

Eilla AI is already seeing early traction in both deal speed and buyer reach. One recent transaction moved from outreach to non-binding offers in around 15 days, with the full process completing within a few months — despite involving multiple companies, shareholders, and a non-obvious buyer. According to Petrov: > “It was a complex deal — multiple companies, multiple shareholders, and a buyer that wouldn’t normally be identified through traditional relationships.” > > Rather than relying on existing networks, the firm identified the buyer through pattern matching at speed against previous acquisitions, surfacing a publicly listed Swedish company that would likely have been missed in a traditional process.

Across its processes so far, Eilla AI reports that around 80 per cent of companies reach the stage of presenting to buyers, suggesting a higher level of early-stage engagement. “In one case, a company that previously secured one NDA with a traditional advisor reached nine NDAs using our process.”

Eilla AI launched its advisory practice at the end of last year and now has around 20 active mandates, with a fee pipeline of approximately €20 million — up more than 15-fold from roughly €1.6 million at the start of the year.

Our Technology Careers [Insights](https://blog.eilla.ai/tag/industry-deep-dives/)

- The provided field_answer attempts a competitive map across Eilla, Bizbe, and Scorta with various dimensions (Primary scope, Geography, Seller preparation, Buyer engine, etc.). However, the field_description task requires exhaustive verification against baselines, explicit changelog, dates, and verifiable source citations for every factual claim across all three companies. The field_answer largely presents asserted claims (and some inferred interpretations) without a complete, source-backed changelog or explicit confirmation/flagging of changes since baseline.
- Completeness check: The answer does not fully cover all requested task items (e.g., it lacks explicit verification flags (CHANGED / CONFIRMED / UNVERIFIED / CONTRADICTED) for each factual claim, and it does not provide a comprehensive, sourced changelog per baseline items). It also does not present a fully exhaustive, source-cited mapping for all three companies across all requested dimensions (legal names, HQ, founding year, funding, product details, deals, lenders, etc.). Therefore, completeness should be false.
- Confidence in field answer relative to excerpts: The field_answer includes several claims that are not directly supported by the provided excerpts (e.g., exact fee percentages varying by company, specific deal mentions, and organizational details with precise phrasing). The excerpts list contains many corroborating items, but the answer’s composite table relies on internal placeholders (e.g., [5_competitive_map_workflow_trust_sba_and_vertical_depth[0]]) that do not map to explicit excerpts or dates. Hence, “supported” should be false.
- Conclusion: Set completeness to false and supported to false. A more robust evaluation would attach explicit per-claim citations from excerpts, provide a detailed changelog against baseline (with timestamps), and clearly mark changed/confirmed/unverified/contradicted statuses for each datapoint.

excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >
Nikola Lazarov, CEO and co-founder, contends that this pace and depth would be impossible to replicate without the infrastructure it has built.

Its proprietary technology, built in-house over three years, combines AI infrastructure with experienced M&A advisors who oversee AI-generated work, manage transaction processes, and coordinate communication between both sides.

Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement. First is preparation. It identifies a broad universe of potential buyers — often larger in SMB deals, where smaller companies attract a wider range of acquirers. “We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > > Next is outreach. While the company utilises its existing relationships, it also deploys highly personalised outreach to new buyers. It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals. This enables it to send highly tailored messages at scale, resulting in higher response rates.

“We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers.
It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals.

Eilla AI’s models are probabilistic, and the system does not rely on generic model outputs or training data alone. Instead, it works with structured context provided by the client, combined with data extracted from proprietary databases and licensed external sources — including a dataset built from tens of millions of scraped pages covering around nine million companies.

Eilla AI’s cost structure is fundamentally different. Because AI handles the volume-intensive work, buyer sourcing, outreach and document creation, the firm operates on a success-fee-only basis with no retainers.
> “In our segment, average deal sizes are around €10–20 million, and we charge about a 5 per cent success fee. So a single deal might generate around €500,000.” > >
Eilla AI’s customer is typically the founder or owner of an SMB business looking to sell.

According to Petrov, two things became clear. First, the M&A industry is quite behind in terms of AI adoption — “even large boutiques were only just integrating tools like ChatGPT internally,” he shared. Second, the SMB segment is underserved. The team decided to combine the AI it has built with the expertise of experienced advisors.

Eilla AI has completed Europe’s first M&A deal executed by an AI-native advisory firm, advising on the acquisition of two Central and Eastern European digital marketing agencies, CreateX and Native Digital, by Swedish listed company [White Pearl Technology Group](https://whitepearltech.com/) .

What “AI-native advisory” means in practice Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement.

The founders of both acquired companies credited Eilla AI with making the transactions possible. “Honestly, without Eilla, this deal would not have happened,” said Aleksandar, founder and CEO of CreateX. The reaction from Native Digital was similar.

Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > >

Eilla AI is already seeing early traction in both deal speed and buyer reach. One recent transaction moved from outreach to non-binding offers in around 15 days, with the full process completing within a few months — despite involving multiple companies, shareholders, and a non-obvious buyer. According to Petrov: > “It was a complex deal — multiple companies, multiple shareholders, and a buyer that wouldn’t normally be identified through traditional relationships.” > > Rather than relying on existing networks, the firm identified the buyer through pattern matching at speed against previous acquisitions, surfacing a publicly listed Swedish company that would likely have been missed in a traditional process.

Across its processes so far, Eilla AI reports that around 80 per cent of companies reach the stage of presenting to buyers, suggesting a higher level of early-stage engagement. “In one case, a company that previously secured one NDA with a traditional advisor reached nine NDAs using our process.”

Eilla AI launched its advisory practice at the end of last year and now has around 20 active mandates, with a fee pipeline of approximately €20 million — up more than 15-fold from roughly €1.6 million at the start of the year.

A British generative AI startup has raised $1.5m (£1.2m) in seed funding to provide automation tools that assist investment firms with deal flow. London-based Eilla AI says its platform “mirrors” industry professionals to carry out tasks such as market mapping, document creation and offer comparisons. “The bottom line is that financial professionals are paid to think, not waste time on mundane tasks,” said Nikola Lazarov, CEO of Eilla AI. “But the amount of time and effort it takes a junior at a financial firm to map out the companies in a specific industry, for example, can spiral quickly.” Eleven Ventures led the seed round, with Fuel Ventures and its founder Mark Pearson (as an angel investor) also taking part. The startup plans to use the seed capital to grow into Europe and America. Eilla AI says over 50 M&A banks, VCs and PE funds have used its financial generative AI software. Svetozar Georgiev, general partner at Eleven Ventures, said: “The daily work of M&A, VC and PE professionals hasn’t evolved much in the past 30 years, dominated by lots of manual data retrieval and analysis, as well as mundane document creation.” Georgiev added that Eilla’s generative AI platform will “provide superhuman productivity” and complete tasks in minutes rather than hours or days.
Eleven Ventures led the seed round, with Fuel Ventures and its founder Mark Pearson (as an angel investor) also taking part.
The startup plans to use the seed capital to grow into Europe and America.

A British generative AI startup has raised $1.5m (£1.2m) in seed funding to provide automation tools that assist investment firms with deal flow. London-based Eilla AI says its platform “mirrors” industry professionals to carry out tasks such as market mapping, document creation and offer comparisons. “The bottom line is that financial professionals are paid to think, not waste time on mundane tasks,” said Nikola Lazarov, CEO of Eilla AI. “But the amount of time and effort it takes a junior at a financial firm to map out the companies in a specific industry, for example, can spiral quickly.” Eleven Ventures led the seed round, with Fuel Ventures and its founder Mark Pearson (as an angel investor) also taking part. The startup plans to use the seed capital to grow into Europe and America. Eilla AI says over 50 M&A banks, VCs and PE funds have used its financial generative AI software. Svetozar Georgiev, general partner at Eleven Ventures, said: “The daily work of M&A, VC and PE professionals hasn’t evolved much in the past 30 years, dominated by lots of manual data retrieval and analysis, as well as mundane document creation.” Georgiev added that Eilla’s generative AI platform will “provide superhuman productivity” and complete tasks in minutes rather than hours or days.

The startup plans to use the seed capital to grow into Europe and America.

excerpts: We are excited to announce Fuel Ventures’ investment into Eilla AI as part of a $1,500,000 seed round, led by Eleven Ventures. [**Eilla AI**](https://eilla.ai/) is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to power the M&A, VC and PE deal workflow by automating mundane tasks and supporting complex decision making.
**What is Eilla AI?**
Eilla AI's technology automates these processes by mirroring industry professionals using generative AI.

The platform also unlocks new insights and supports complex decision-making through aggregation and analysis of large amounts of information from various sources in significantly less time than is currently possible.

This funding will be vital as we aim to expand our technical team and product offering, while also positioning the business for growth across the M&A, venture capital, and private equity markets.” **Nikola Lazarov, CEO at Eilla AI.**

We are excited to be leading Eilla AI’s seed funding round and work with its talented team, which uniquely combines deep AI expertise with M&A domain knowledge.”_ **_Eleven Ventures General Partner, Svetozar Georgiev_** _._
A huge congratulations to founders Nikola Lazarov, Nikolay Babulkov and Petar Petrov - we can’t wait to build something great together.

CEO Nikola Lazarov: An AI engineer, former Hedge Fund quant, experience as an early employee at a YC backed startup and a Masters in Generative AI from the University of Cambridge CTO Nikolay Babulkov: An AI engineer with 7 years experience across ML, software and DevOps and papers published at NLP conferences (ACL and CLEF) CCO Petar Petrov: Experience across sales and marketing at high growth startups, including being the Growth Lead at B2B SaaS company Vita Mojo, helping them land a $30m Series B from Battery Ventures.

To date, Eilla AI has been used by advisors and investors from more than 50 M&A banks and VC and PE funds to help optimise specific tasks by researching, aggregating, and analysing information from key industry sources and internal data.
We tackle this problem by analysing all of the essential information and then providing a report in the appropriate format for our clients.

Buying or selling a business is one of the biggest moves you’ll make. Bizbe pairs AI with experienced brokers to run the whole transaction, so you always know exactly where you stand.

Do I have to use Bizbe for the entire process? Bizbe is built to run the whole transaction end to end — valuation, listing, offers, diligence, and close — with our team alongside you. That guided, all-in-one approach is what keeps deals fast and transparent.

01 Day 1 Get a free, data-backed valuation Create an account and answer a few questions. Our AI benchmarks your business against comparable closed deals, so you start with a real number — no cost, no obligation. 02 Week 1 List privately to vetted buyers Your business is shown only to identity-verified buyers with proof of funds. You stay confidential until you decide to engage. 03 Weeks 2–6 Field offers in one live deal room Watch interest, offers, and LOIs arrive in real time. Your deal team helps you read each one and respond with confidence. 04 Weeks 6–10 Run diligence with support We coordinate documents, data-room access, and the back-and-forth so the process keeps moving and nothing stalls. 05 Close Close — and only then pay Sign, transfer, and get paid. Our success fee comes due only when your sale completes.

What does Bizbe cost? Starting is free — valuing your business, listing it, or getting verified as a buyer costs nothing. We charge a single, transparent success fee that's agreed up front and only due when your sale actually completes.

Free to start Value your business, list it, or browse and get verified as a buyer — all at no cost. No listing fees It costs nothing to be on Bizbe. We don't charge for being listed or for staying listed. Success fee at close A single, transparent fee, agreed up front and due only when your sale actually completes.
Success fee at close A single, transparent fee, agreed up front and due only when your sale actually completes.

How are buyers vetted? Every buyer completes identity verification (KYC) and a proof-of-funds check before they can view full financials or enter a data room. It keeps conversations serious and protects your sensitive information.
02 Week 1 List privately to vetted buyers Your business is shown only to identity-verified buyers with proof of funds. You stay confidential until you decide to engage.

Who can see my business when I list it? Only identity-verified buyers with proof of funds. Your listing stays confidential by default: you control what shows publicly and what unlocks only after a buyer signs an NDA.
03 Weeks 2–6 Field offers in one live deal room Watch interest, offers, and LOIs arrive in real time. Your deal team helps you read each one and respond with confidence.

What kinds of businesses are on Bizbe? Established, cash-flowing Main Street and lower-middle-market businesses — from service and logistics companies to local operators. If you're not sure whether yours is a fit, a free valuation is the quickest way to find out.

FAQ Questions, answered. How long does it take to sell a business? It varies with size and complexity, but most Bizbe sales move from listing to close in roughly two to four months — far faster than the year-plus a traditional brokerage often takes. Because everyone is verified up front and the process runs on one platform, there is far less waiting and chasing.

excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >

excerpts: We are excited to announce Fuel Ventures’ investment into Eilla AI as part of a $1,500,000 seed round, led by Eleven Ventures. [**Eilla AI**](https://eilla.ai/) is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to power the M&A, VC and PE deal workflow by automating mundane tasks and supporting complex decision making.
**What is Eilla AI?**
Eilla AI's technology automates these processes by mirroring industry professionals using generative AI.

The platform also unlocks new insights and supports complex decision-making through aggregation and analysis of large amounts of information from various sources in significantly less time than is currently possible.

This funding will be vital as we aim to expand our technical team and product offering, while also positioning the business for growth across the M&A, venture capital, and private equity markets.” **Nikola Lazarov, CEO at Eilla AI.**

We are excited to be leading Eilla AI’s seed funding round and work with its talented team, which uniquely combines deep AI expertise with M&A domain knowledge.”_ **_Eleven Ventures General Partner, Svetozar Georgiev_** _._
A huge congratulations to founders Nikola Lazarov, Nikolay Babulkov and Petar Petrov - we can’t wait to build something great together.

CEO Nikola Lazarov: An AI engineer, former Hedge Fund quant, experience as an early employee at a YC backed startup and a Masters in Generative AI from the University of Cambridge CTO Nikolay Babulkov: An AI engineer with 7 years experience across ML, software and DevOps and papers published at NLP conferences (ACL and CLEF) CCO Petar Petrov: Experience across sales and marketing at high growth startups, including being the Growth Lead at B2B SaaS company Vita Mojo, helping them land a $30m Series B from Battery Ventures.

To date, Eilla AI has been used by advisors and investors from more than 50 M&A banks and VC and PE funds to help optimise specific tasks by researching, aggregating, and analysing information from key industry sources and internal data.
We tackle this problem by analysing all of the essential information and then providing a report in the appropriate format for our clients.

We are excited to announce Fuel Ventures’ investment into Eilla AI as part of a $1,500,000 seed round, led by Eleven Ventures. [**Eilla AI**](https://eilla.ai/) is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to power the M&A, VC and PE deal workflow by automating mundane tasks and supporting complex decision making. A huge congratulations to founders Nikola Lazarov, Nikolay Babulkov and Petar Petrov - we can’t wait to build something great together.

Our Story We spent years building AI for the world's top M&A firms. And along the way, we saw a market that's been underserved. Below a certain company size, corners get cut and quality gets sacrificed - not because advisors don't care, but because the fees can't carry the large teams needed to run a top-tier process. AI breaks that constraint. So we built an AI-native M&A advisory from the ground up - designed to give SMBs the quality of service reserved for billion-dollar deals, delivering higher-value exits.

How it works One platform, a real deal team, nothing hidden. Buying or selling a business is one of the biggest moves you’ll make. Bizbe pairs AI with experienced brokers to run the whole transaction, so you always know exactly where you stand. The path is built so you always know what happens next and who’s handling it. I'm selling I'm buying 01 Day 1 Get a free, data-backed valuation Create an account and answer a few questions. Our AI benchmarks your business against comparable closed deals, so you start with a real number — no cost, no obligation. 02 Week 1 List privately to vetted buyers Your business is shown only to identity-verified buyers with proof of funds. excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >
Nikola Lazarov, CEO and co-founder, contends that this pace and depth would be impossible to replicate without the infrastructure it has built.

Its proprietary technology, built in-house over three years, combines AI infrastructure with experienced M&A advisors who oversee AI-generated work, manage transaction processes, and coordinate communication between both sides.

Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement. First is preparation. It identifies a broad universe of potential buyers — often larger in SMB deals, where smaller companies attract a wider range of acquirers. “We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > > Next is outreach. While the company utilises its existing relationships, it also deploys highly personalised outreach to new buyers. It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals. This enables it to send highly tailored messages at scale, resulting in higher response rates.

“We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers.
It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals.

Eilla AI’s models are probabilistic, and the system does not rely on generic model outputs or training data alone. Instead, it works with structured context provided by the client, combined with data extracted from proprietary databases and licensed external sources — including a dataset built from tens of millions of scraped pages covering around nine million companies.

Eilla AI’s cost structure is fundamentally different. Because AI handles the volume-intensive work, buyer sourcing, outreach and document creation, the firm operates on a success-fee-only basis with no retainers.

According to Petrov, two things became clear. First, the M&A industry is quite behind in terms of AI adoption — “even large boutiques were only just integrating tools like ChatGPT internally,” he shared. Second, the SMB segment is underserved. The team decided to combine the AI it has built with the expertise of experienced advisors.

Eilla AI has completed Europe’s first M&A deal executed by an AI-native advisory firm, advising on the acquisition of two Central and Eastern European digital marketing agencies, CreateX and Native Digital, by Swedish listed company [White Pearl Technology Group](https://whitepearltech.com/) .

Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement.

The founders of both acquired companies credited Eilla AI with making the transactions possible. “Honestly, without Eilla, this deal would not have happened,” said Aleksandar, founder and CEO of CreateX. The reaction from Native Digital was similar.

Assessment rationale:
- The field_description task asks for a exhaustive, structured, source-cited competitive map update on Eilla, Bizbe, and Scorta, including verification of baselines, updated factual claims, and a structured, source-backed output with a changelog. The provided field_answer is a qualitative, high-level synthesis in a five-dimension table form, with some comparative conclusions and citations placeholders (e.g., [synthesis[0]]). It does not present an explicit, exhaustive, claim-by-claim verification or a formal changelog, nor does it enumerate the full set of required attributes for each company (legal names, URLs, HQ, founding year, stage, headcount, funding details with dates, product pages and pricing, deals, GTM channels, partnerships, tech claims, etc.) in a structured, source-backed format. 
- The excerpts supplied do include numerous source-based data points that could be used to validate or contradict the baselines (eilla.ai/eilla.com; bizbe.com; scorta.ai/app; Tech.eu article on Eilla; Bizbe disclosures; Scorta about page and ExitIQ pages; etc.). The field_answer, however, does not systematically map each requirement to explicit excerpts or present a formal change log per claim. 
- Therefore, completeness is false because the answer does not fully address all required aspects in a traceable, claim-by-claim, sourced manner. 
- Supported by excerpts: Several excerpts explicitly back key claims in the synthesized output (e.g., Eilla’s 5% fee, seed funding; Bizbe 6.99% success fee and disclosures; Scorta 0% commission, ExitIQ details; CreateX/Native deal, etc.). The presence of these sources means the high-level conclusions could be supported, but the field_answer itself does not present a structured, complete extraction per the prompt’s task. 
- Conclusion: completeness = false; supported = true (the answer aligns with data present in excerpts, though not exhaustively or in fully structured form).

Bizbe Bizbe The AI-native brokerage making it easier to buy and sell Main Street businesses.

How it works One platform, a real deal team, nothing hidden. Buying or selling a business is one of the biggest moves you’ll make. Bizbe pairs AI with experienced brokers to run the whole transaction, so you always know exactly where you stand. [Get started for free](https://app.bizbe.com/sign-up) See the steps Free to start Verified on both sides You only pay at close A deal, end to end Guided throughout 01 Value A real, data-backed number 02 Match Vetted buyers, private listings 03 Diligence One organized data room 04 Close You only pay on completion The journey Five clear steps, whichever side you’re on. The path is built so you always know what happens next and who’s handling it. I'm selling I'm buying 01 Day 1 Get a free, data-backed valuation Create an account and answer a few questions. Our AI benchmarks your business against comparable closed deals, so you start with a real number — no cost, no obligation. 02 Week 1 List privately to vetted buyers Your business is shown only to identity-verified buyers with proof of funds. You stay confidential until you decide to engage. 03 Weeks 2–6 Field offers in one live deal room Watch interest, offers, and LOIs arrive in real time. Your deal team helps you read each one and respond with confidence. 04 Weeks 6–10 Run diligence with support We coordinate documents, data-room access, and the back-and-forth so the process keeps moving and nothing stalls. 05 Close Close — and only then pay Sign, transfer, and get paid. Our success fee comes due only when your sale completes. [Get your free valuation](https://app.bizbe.com/sign-up) What powers it Software speed. Human judgment. A listings board leaves you on your own. A traditional broker is slow and opaque. Bizbe gives you both at once: AI for the heavy lifting, real people for the decisions that matter. The platform Handles the busywork Benchmarks your valuation against comparable closed deals Matches the right buyers to the right businesses Keeps financials and documents organized in one data room Tracks every offer and milestone in real time Nudges the process forward so nothing goes quiet Your deal team Handles the judgment Positions your business so the right buyers take notice Reads every offer with you and flags what matters Guides diligence and answers the hard questions Negotiates terms with your goals front and center Drives the deal to a clean, fully-papered close Trust & confidentiality Built so both sides can move with confidence. Selling or buying a business means sharing sensitive numbers. Bizbe is engineered to protect them at every step. Verified on both sides Every buyer clears identity (KYC) and proof-of-funds before they see financials. Every seller is a real business we've spoken with. No tire-kickers, no time-wasters. Private by default Your listing stays confidential. You control what shows publicly and what unlocks only after a verified buyer signs an NDA. A controlled data room Share financials and documents in one organized place, with access you grant per buyer and can revoke at any time. Pricing You only pay when the deal closes. Our incentives are simple: we don’t get paid unless you do. That keeps everyone focused on getting to a great outcome, not racking up retainers. Free to start Value your business, list it, or browse and get verified as a buyer — all at no cost. No listing fees It costs nothing to be on Bizbe. We don't charge for being listed or for staying listed. Success fee at close A single, transparent fee, agreed up front and due only when your sale actually completes. Starting is free — valuing your business, listing it, or getting verified as a buyer costs nothing. We charge a single, transparent success fee that's agreed up front and only due when your sale actually completes. Who can see my business when I list it? Only identity-verified buyers with proof of funds. Your listing stays confidential by default: you control what shows publicly and what unlocks only after a buyer signs an NDA. How are buyers vetted? Every buyer completes identity verification (KYC) and a proof-of-funds check before they can view full financials or enter a data room. It keeps conversations serious and protects your sensitive information. What kinds of businesses are on Bizbe? Established, cash-flowing Main Street and lower-middle-market businesses — from service and logistics companies to local operators. excerpts: Eilla AI was founded in 2022.
I spoke to Petar Petrov, Chief Commercial Officer and co-founder of Eilla AI, to learn more.
> “We partnered with our Head of M&A, Dmitry, a senior investment banker with over 13 years of experience at firms like Jefferies and Citibank.” > >
Nikola Lazarov, CEO and co-founder, contends that this pace and depth would be impossible to replicate without the infrastructure it has built.

Its proprietary technology, built in-house over three years, combines AI infrastructure with experienced M&A advisors who oversee AI-generated work, manage transaction processes, and coordinate communication between both sides.

Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement. First is preparation. It identifies a broad universe of potential buyers — often larger in SMB deals, where smaller companies attract a wider range of acquirers. “We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > > Next is outreach. While the company utilises its existing relationships, it also deploys highly personalised outreach to new buyers. It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals. This enables it to send highly tailored messages at scale, resulting in higher response rates.

“We use AI to identify these buyers. Eilla has built a large proprietary database with detailed information on companies, and uses AI to identify the right buyers from that database based on similar deals and synergies,” explained Petrov. Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers.
It built a database of around nine million companies, tracking their products, tech, and other signals.

Eilla AI’s models are probabilistic, and the system does not rely on generic model outputs or training data alone. Instead, it works with structured context provided by the client, combined with data extracted from proprietary databases and licensed external sources — including a dataset built from tens of millions of scraped pages covering around nine million companies.

Eilla AI’s cost structure is fundamentally different. Because AI handles the volume-intensive work, buyer sourcing, outreach and document creation, the firm operates on a success-fee-only basis with no retainers.
> “In our segment, average deal sizes are around €10–20 million, and we charge about a 5 per cent success fee. So a single deal might generate around €500,000.” > >
Eilla AI’s customer is typically the founder or owner of an SMB business looking to sell.

According to Petrov, two things became clear. First, the M&A industry is quite behind in terms of AI adoption — “even large boutiques were only just integrating tools like ChatGPT internally,” he shared. Second, the SMB segment is underserved. The team decided to combine the AI it has built with the expertise of experienced advisors.

Eilla AI has completed Europe’s first M&A deal executed by an AI-native advisory firm, advising on the acquisition of two Central and Eastern European digital marketing agencies, CreateX and Native Digital, by Swedish listed company [White Pearl Technology Group](https://whitepearltech.com/) .

What “AI-native advisory” means in practice Eilla AI’s technology enables it to reach hundreds of high-fit buyers across multiple countries within days, each with messaging built on in-depth research into what makes the acquisition compelling for that specific buyer. Eilla AI runs a structured process similar to what top-tier investment banks use, but applied to the SMB market. The AI handles large parts of the workflow, but humans step in where full automation isn’t yet reliable — especially for customisation and judgement.

The founders of both acquired companies credited Eilla AI with making the transactions possible. “Honestly, without Eilla, this deal would not have happened,” said Aleksandar, founder and CEO of CreateX. The reaction from Native Digital was similar.

Eilla uses its AI automations to build key materials, including the confidential information memorandum (CIM), the core document used to present the business to potential buyers. > “Traditionally, this process can take one to two months. We can do it in a few days.” > >

Eilla AI is already seeing early traction in both deal speed and buyer reach. One recent transaction moved from outreach to non-binding offers in around 15 days, with the full process completing within a few months — despite involving multiple companies, shareholders, and a non-obvious buyer. According to Petrov: > “It was a complex deal — multiple companies, multiple shareholders, and a buyer that wouldn’t normally be identified through traditional relationships.” > > Rather than relying on existing networks, the firm identified the buyer through pattern matching at speed against previous acquisitions, surfacing a publicly listed Swedish company that would likely have been missed in a traditional process.

Across its processes so far, Eilla AI reports that around 80 per cent of companies reach the stage of presenting to buyers, suggesting a higher level of early-stage engagement. “In one case, a company that previously secured one NDA with a traditional advisor reached nine NDAs using our process.”

Eilla AI launched its advisory practice at the end of last year and now has around 20 active mandates, with a fee pipeline of approximately €20 million — up more than 15-fold from roughly €1.6 million at the start of the year.
