content.executive_insights:
- **Proof Hierarchy**: Eilla has the strongest public transaction evidence: a named CreateX and Native Digital sale to White Pearl Technology Group, an offer in about 15 days and approximately 6x EBITDA in the company case study. [executive_insights[0]] [3] -> Treat Eilla as the most proven sell-side competitor, while separating one verified deal from its broader performance claims.
- **Scale Signal**: Eilla's current product copy says 8M company profiles, while an April 8, 2026 Tech.eu article said approximately 9M companies and tens of millions of scraped pages. [executive_insights[1]] [22][executive_insights[2]] [2] -> Use "approximately 8M to 9M" as a disclosed database range, not as evidence of growth or decline.
- **Fee Transparency**: Bizbe moved from an undisclosed success fee in the baseline to a current legal disclosure of a USD 2,500 seller onboarding package and a standard 6.99% seller success fee, while buyer representation is disclosed at USD 1,500 per month. [executive_insights[3]] [20] -> Model Bizbe as a priced brokerage, not a free marketplace.
- **Main Street Workflow**: Bizbe publicly describes a valuation-to-close workflow with private listings, KYC, proof of funds, live rooms and diligence, and its listings page showed six opportunities with its deal team when reviewed. [executive_insights[4]] [5][executive_insights[5]] [16] -> It is the clearest public broker operating system, but the small visible inventory makes product maturity and throughput uncertain.
- **Readiness Ownership**: Scorta is the only company whose public product explicitly turns pre-listing readiness into a product: valuation range, offer scenarios, SBA pre-screen, 90-day fix list and lender-review staging. [executive_insights[6]] [9] -> Scorta owns the most distinctive white-space thesis, but buyers should demand live customer and lender evidence before treating the claims as proven.
- **Funding Confidence**: Eilla's USD 1.5M November 2023 seed led by Eleven Ventures and involving Fuel Ventures is corroborated by Fuel and independent coverage. [executive_insights[7]] [29][executive_insights[8]] [31] -> Bizbe and Scorta should be modeled as funding-unverified: Tracxn returned no company row for either search, and no formal round or named amount was located. [executive_insights[9]] [33]
- **Agent Depth**: Eilla documents AI research, buyer matching, CIM production and data-room support with senior advisor review; Scorta documents classified files, logged actions, qualification and human approval; Bizbe describes AI paired with experienced brokers. [executive_insights[1]] [22][executive_insights[6]] [9][executive_insights[4]] [5] -> All three publicly support human-in-the-loop automation; none publicly proves autonomous work inside lender portals or external VDRs.
- **Home-Services Proof**: Scorta has the clearest public home-services artifact, an illustrative Atlas HVAC example; Bizbe claims home-services relevance but its six public opportunities did not expose a category mix; Eilla's public pages reviewed here did not establish home-services traction. [executive_insights[6]] [9][executive_insights[5]] [16] -> Scorta leads on positioning, not yet on independently verified volume or closed deals.
- **Immediate White Space**: No reviewed public source proves a competitor combining continuous sale-readiness scoring, deterministic financial recasting, named SBA lender execution, no-exclusivity distribution and wholesale-ready broker packages at sub-USD 2M deal sizes. -> That is the clearest opening, but it remains a product opportunity rather than a verified Scorta capability.
content.1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unans:
This map distinguishes four conditions. **Confirmed** means a primary company, legal, or reputable contemporaneous source states the fact. **Changed** means the current evidence differs from the supplied baseline. **Unverified** means the claim may be true but was not supported by the public sources reviewed. **Contradicted** means a current disclosure conflicts with the baseline or with another current company page. Marketing claims are retained as company claims, not upgraded to independent facts.

| Company | Strongest current proof | Evidence quality | Main unanswered questions as of 2026-08-17 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eilla AI | UK legal record, corroborated seed, official product pages, April 2026 named transaction and fee/pipeline disclosure. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[0]] [32][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[1]] [29][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[2]] [3][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[3]] [2] | High for identity, funding and one deal; medium for operating metrics | Current team size beyond the Tracxn signal of 10, any post-April deal, US expansion, home-services traction, sub-USD 5M pricing, and independent valuation uplift remain unverified. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[4]] [33][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[5]] [14] |
| Bizbe | Current legal disclosures, founders page, LinkedIn company profile, transaction workflow and six visible opportunities. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[6]] [20][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[7]] [4][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[8]] [12][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[9]] [16] | High for legal terms and founder identities; medium for product operation | Funding, Shark Tank connection, state brokerage licenses, exact FedEx sales claim, home-services inventory, and independently verified closed deals remain unresolved. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[10]] [11][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[4]] [33] |
| Scorta | Public Scorta app, About page and DealIQ page with named founders, product modules, pricing language and illustrative workflow. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[11]] [8][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[12]] [9][1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[13]] [10] | Medium for what the company says it is building; low for independent traction and capitalization | Legal entity, location, funding, YC profile, headcount, customers, closed deals, lender partners and claimed data-system integrations were not publicly established. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[4]] [33] |

The most important unanswered issues are not cosmetic. They determine whether each company is a functioning transaction intermediary, a software product, or a well-designed thesis. For Eilla, the gap is incremental proof after its first disclosed deal. For Bizbe, it is whether the transaction room and FedEx specialization translate into repeatable closings. For Scorta, it is whether the readiness workflow is deployed with lenders and buyers rather than only demonstrated in product copy.

A second evidence limitation is that company pages often combine product facts and outcome claims. Eilla's funnel says 8M companies screened, 300 buyers contacted, 20 NDAs, eight management meetings and five competitive offers, but it does not state a completed-deal count in that funnel. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[14]] [22] Scorta publishes a 38-day intake-to-LOI average, 100% buyer qualification before LOI, and a 20% to 30% close-rate comparison, while also labeling its values illustrative. [1_evidence_ledger_and_what_remains_unanswered[12]] [9] These are useful hypotheses for diligence, not independently audited benchmarks.
content.2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_:
### Identity, team and capital

Eilla AI is legally EILLA AI LTD, company number 14201306. The Companies House record shows an active private limited company with a London registered office, incorporated on June 28, 2022, and classified under software and information technology. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[0]] [32] Tracxn lists London, a 2022 founding year, Seed stage and an official employee count of 10. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[1]] [33] The legal record supports the London identity and founding year, but the supplied detail that the business began in Veliko Tarnovo and later relocated to London was not independently established in the current evidence.

Fuel Ventures and UK Tech coverage corroborate a USD 1.5M seed round in November 2023 led by Eleven Ventures, with Fuel Ventures and Mark Pearson also participating. The named founders are Nikola Lazarov, Nikolay Babulkov and Petar Petrov, serving as CEO, CTO and CCO respectively. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[2]] [29][2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[3]] [31] Lazarov's current public profile identifies him as co-founder and CEO, and a podcast profile describes his earlier work as a quant at London hedge fund Marble Bar Asset Management. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[4]] [25][2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[5]] [34] The supplied Cambridge generative-AI degree, Babulkov's ACL/CLEF pedigree and Petar Petrov's Vita Mojo history were not all re-established from the current primary pages, so they should remain medium-confidence background rather than core competitive facts.

Eilla's careers page is a hiring signal rather than a headcount disclosure. It lists experienced advisors with at least seven years of investment-banking experience, analysts and associates with two or more years, engineers at all levels, and operations, commercial growth and product roles. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[6]] [19] The page does not name a complete team. Dmitry Zaporozhskiy is identified by Tech.eu as Head of M&A with more than 13 years at Jefferies and Citibank. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] The best public headcount signal is therefore Tracxn's 10, not a company-confirmed August 2026 number.

### Product and proof of execution

Eilla positions itself as an AI-native M&A advisory for SMBs. Its current product page says AI supports the full M&A process while senior advisors lead and review every step. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[8]] [22] The workflow includes company-file ingestion and missing-data flags, equity-story development, AI-generated CIM and teaser materials, buyer research, buyer matching, data-room analysis, missing-workstream tracking and buyer-question support. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[8]] [22] This is broader than an AI valuation widget: the company is selling a human-led sell-side mandate with automation around research, materials and process management.

The strongest proof is the CreateX and Native Digital transaction. Eilla's case study says the two Bulgarian digital agencies were acquired by Swedish-listed White Pearl Technology Group, with an offer within 15 days and approximately 6x EBITDA. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[9]] [3] Tech.eu describes it as Europe's first AI-native M&A deal and dates its coverage April 8, 2026. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] That supports one named transaction, not the stronger baseline claim that Eilla has already demonstrated a general six-to-eight-week sale cycle. The article does support CIM production in a few days versus the one-to-two-month conventional process and outreach to non-binding offers in about 15 days. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2]

| Eilla disclosure | Current evidence | Competitive interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Company database | Current product copy says 8M profiles; April coverage says approximately 9M companies and tens of millions of scraped pages. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[8]] [22][2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] | Large proprietary-data positioning, but the 8M/9M discrepancy is a definition or copy issue, not a verified trend. |
| Buyer funnel | 8M screened, 300 contacted, 20 NDAs, eight management meetings and five competitive offers. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[8]] [22] | Strong transparency on a funnel example; completed deals are not stated. |
| Process speed | Materials in days, outreach to non-binding offers in about 15 days; full process described as a few months. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] | More credible than an unsupported end-to-end six-week promise, but still company-reported. |
| Valuation and NDA claims | Approximately 6x EBITDA in the named case; one case is described as one NDA leading to nine NDAs; 80% reach buyer presentation. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[9]] [3][2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] | Useful deal-level signals, not a statistically defined uplift or conversion study. |
| Revenue model | Success-fee-only, no retainers; average deal size stated as EUR 10M to EUR 20M and fee approximately 5%, or about EUR 500K on a typical deal. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] | Optimized for larger lower-middle-market mandates, not obviously for sub-USD 2M Main Street deals. |

The website does now explicitly address businesses under EUR 5M in revenue, but the reviewed public pages did not expose a fee schedule or a distinct lighter-track product page; a guessed standalone URL returned 404. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[10]] [6][2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[11]] [14] The baseline's under-USD 5M fee schedule therefore remains unverified. The same applies to the baseline's 25% higher valuation claim, the six-to-12-month to under-six-to-eight-week comparison, US expansion, home-services traction and any post-April 2026 deal announcement.

### Pipeline and strategic position

The April 2026 Tech.eu article reported approximately 20 active mandates, about EUR 20M in fee pipeline and growth from approximately EUR 1.6M at the start of the year. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[7]] [2] This materially confirms the baseline's pipeline direction, but it is a dated snapshot and should not be treated as the August 2026 current pipeline. Eilla's current homepage instead emphasizes the funnel and the eight-million-company database. [2_eilla_ai_the_most_proven_sell_side_ai_story[8]] [22]

Eilla's moat is therefore a combination of high-ticket advisory credibility, buyer-data infrastructure and a human M&A team. Its weakness in this comparison is not the product concept; it is the absence of public proof that the same machine works in small home-services transactions, integrates SBA underwriting or turns an owner into a continuously sellable asset before a mandate begins.
content.3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brok:
### Identity, founders and economics

Bizbe's current legal disclosures identify the business as Bizbe, Inc., with the disclosures effective June 26, 2026. The document says Bizbe connects buyers, sellers and brokers but is not a party to the underlying transaction. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[0]] [20] LinkedIn currently lists New York, New York as headquarters, company size of 2 to 10 employees, a 2025 founding year, and Eric Trevino, Eddie H and Stephen as visible team members. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[1]] [12] This changes the baseline's Miami-first description: Miami may still be an operating location or branding signal, but the current public company profile supports New York more directly, and Monterrey was not confirmed in the reviewed evidence.

The About page identifies Stephen McKinney as co-founder and CEO. It says he started and exited two operating businesses and sold his first company through a traditional broker, motivating the transparency thesis. It identifies Eddie Hudson as co-founder and CTO, with 15 years of software experience and a recently sold software-consulting company. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[2]] [4] This resolves the baseline's incomplete "Eddie" name: the public name is Eddie Hudson. A separate profile describes McKinney's Retty Logistics background, including 170 full- and part-time workers and 80 delivery vehicles, but that is a biography claim and not proof of Bizbe's current transaction volume. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[3]] [11]

No formal financing round, amount or Shark Tank-affiliated investor was corroborated. Tracxn returned no Bizbe company row in the targeted query. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[4]] [33] That is not proof that Bizbe has no capital; it means the funding thesis should be labeled unverified rather than reported as a round. The company appears founder-led and early-stage from the public 2-to-10 employee signal, but employee count itself is not a current legal disclosure. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[1]] [12]

The largest baseline change is pricing. Bizbe's current disclosures specify a USD 2,500 seller onboarding package for deal documents and marketing, a standard seller success fee of 6.99% of total transaction value at closing, and USD 1,500 per month for buyer representation. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[0]] [20] The homepage says free to start, a small one-time documents fee, a success fee at close and no buyer fee. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[5]] [7] The legal terms and marketing page are therefore internally inconsistent. The defensible map is: seller onboarding is not fully free, seller success pricing is now publicly disclosed at 6.99%, and buyer representation may be paid when a buyer elects that service.

### Product and operating evidence

Bizbe describes a five-stage workflow: free valuation, private vetted listing, offer collection in a live room, diligence and close. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5] It says buyers pass KYC and proof-of-funds checks before seeing full financials or data-room content. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5] It also positions experienced brokers alongside AI across the whole transaction rather than selling an automated valuation alone. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5] The disclosed timing is Day 1 valuation, Week 1 listing, Weeks 2 to 6 offers, Weeks 6 to 10 diligence, and close thereafter, with listing-to-close described elsewhere as two to four months. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5]

The listings page showed six opportunities with the deal team, updated weekly, while requiring a free account, identity check and proof of funds to unlock deeper information. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[7]] [16] That is meaningful evidence of a functioning inventory surface, but the public page did not disclose a reliable category split. It therefore cannot establish how much inventory is home services versus FedEx ISP or linehaul logistics. The baseline's home-services specialization is plausible as a target segment but unverified as current volume.

| Bizbe feature or claim | Current status | What a buyer or competitor should infer |
|---|---|---|
| AI valuation and transaction workflow | Confirmed as product positioning, with AI plus experienced brokers from valuation through close. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5] | More complete than a listings-only marketplace, but public proof of closed volume is limited. |
| KYC and proof of funds | Confirmed as stated gate before full financials and data room. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5] | A concrete trust and access-control feature, not merely a marketing statement about qualified buyers. |
| Live deal room | Confirmed as the stated offer and diligence interface. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5] | Product maturity is still unverified because no external buyer or seller audit was found. |
| Current inventory | Six opportunities with the deal team when reviewed. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[7]] [16] | A measurable supply signal, but not a volume or close-rate metric. |
| FedEx ISP sales | The company and content emphasize logistics and FedEx ISP, but the USD 10M-plus closed-sales claim was not independently corroborated in the reviewed sources. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[6]] [5][3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[5]] [7] | Treat FedEx expertise and the USD 10M figure as company claims until named transactions or seller references are provided. |
| Fees | USD 2,500 onboarding, 6.99% seller success fee and USD 1,500/month buyer representation in legal disclosures. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[0]] [20] | A transparent headline rate exists, but buyer and seller pages need reconciliation. |

The legal disclosures also say Bizbe does not provide legal, financial, tax, accounting or investment advice; listing information is seller-provided and not independently audited; AI output may be inaccurate; and outcomes are not guaranteed. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[0]] [20] These limitations are not a weakness by themselves. They are useful evidence that the product is a broker and workflow layer, not a substitute for diligence or a regulated investment bank.

### GTM, licensing and partnerships

Bizbe's content strategy is founder-oriented: the blog describes practical guides, market reads and owner stories written founder-to-founder, with an August 13, 2026 post focused on private-sale preparation through close. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[8]] [1] Search-visible content also targets FedEx ISP valuation, SBA eligibility, SDE valuation and diligence questions. This is a focused SEO and education funnel for owners who may otherwise search for a broker, not broad enterprise M&A thought leadership.

The reviewed sources did not verify state-by-state business-broker licenses, a formal FedEx partnership, a named SBA lender, a CPA channel or a Shark Tank investor. The absence is a diligence gap, not proof that no license or relationship exists. Bizbe's public positioning as a "trusted investment bank" for FedEx ISP is also in tension with its current legal statement that it is a broker and is not a party to transactions. [3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[5]] [7][3_bizbe_a_more_concrete_main_street_brokerage_operating_system[0]] [20] The legal characterization should control the competitive map.
content.4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_:
### What is public

Scorta's public app calls the company "an AI-native broker for Main Street" and says it is "Backed by Combinator." [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] Its About page names Suyash Agrawal as co-founder and CEO, with two years running a private-equity firm acquiring Main Street businesses, and Puneet Gupta as co-founder and CTO, described as a builder focused on an AI-native product. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[1]] [8] The About page describes a 2024-25 thesis, late-2025 building, a March 2026 ExitIQ launch and current active deals. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[1]] [8]

The public evidence does not establish a legal entity, HQ, funding amount, capitalization date, headcount, independent customer list or named closing. A targeted Tracxn query returned no Scorta row. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[2]] [33] I also did not locate a company-specific YC directory profile or funding announcement that corroborates the page's "Backed by Combinator" phrase. That phrase should be reported as a company claim, not as confirmed Y Combinator backing. ExitIQ is the seller-side readiness product; DealIQ is presented as a buyer-side engine. An unrelated exitiq.com exit-planning site should not be conflated with Scorta.

### Product, pricing and readiness mechanism

Scorta's strongest differentiation is that it starts before listing. Its public Gap Report promises a valuation range, three offer scenarios, an SBA pre-screen, a 90-day fix list and comparable closed deals. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] The About page frames readiness across financial clarity, owner dependency, operational documentation and SBA financability. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[1]] [8] The app says files are classified, redacted and staged for buyer diligence and lender review, with NDA flow, buyer qualification, diligence Q&A, human approval and a logged action history. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9]

That is a materially different mechanism from Eilla's sell-side mandate and Bizbe's transaction room. Scorta is attempting to make a business continuously saleable and financeable before it routes the opportunity to buyers or brokers. The public page says ExitIQ is free, requires no login, takes about three minutes and avoids a 10% broker fee. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] It also advertises 0% commission and an approximately 3% flat success fee. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] This is a current public price signal, but not evidence of the historical internal approximately 5% fee or of an actually collected fee on a closed deal.

| Scorta public element | Evidence | Confidence and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Seller readiness | Valuation, offer scenarios, SBA pre-screen, 90-day fix list and comparable deals. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] | High confidence that this is the public product thesis; low confidence on delivered outcomes. |
| Workflow controls | Classification, redaction, staged files, NDA, qualification, Q&A, human approval and logged actions. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] | Stronger agentic-workflow description than a simple AI copywriter; no public integration proof. |
| Illustrative home-services use case | Atlas HVAC LLC in Tampa, Florida with a USD 1.4M to USD 2.1M sample valuation range, an SBA likelihood label and a 4 minute 12 second report time. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] | Demonstrates the intended UX, not a verified customer transaction. The page labels the values illustrative. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] |
| Buyer product | DealIQ turns a pasted listing into a deal card, screen score and PASS/DIG/PURSUE flow, with addback analysis, capital-stack and debt-service analysis, cash-on-cash and a price slider. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[3]] [10] | Clear buyer-side concept; public roadmap language still places buyer-side product in Q4. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[3]] [10] |
| Outcome claims | Approximately 38 days intake to LOI, 100% buyer qualification before LOI, 186-day traditional median time on market and 20% to 30% close-rate comparison. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] | Company-reported and apparently benchmark-style claims; no independent cohort or deal list found. |
| Roadmap | Negotiation Table Q3, Buyer-Side Product Q4 and Transaction Infrastructure 2026. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[0]] [9] | Product direction, not proof that each module was live by August 2026. |

Scorta's public product is therefore more specific than the baseline thesis in some respects, especially the no-login diagnostic, Gap Report, staged diligence and logged human approval. It is less proven than the internal thesis implies in other respects: no public evidence was found for QBO, Gusto, Stripe, POS, lender-portal, CPA or named SBA-lender integrations. The claimed "lender review" staging is not the same as lender underwriting or a lender partnership.

The critical diligence question is whether Scorta has a repeatable supply-and-demand loop. The About page says active deals, but no public page reviewed names a seller, buyer, lender or completed transaction. [4_scorta_readiness_first_product_thesis_thin_external_proof[1]] [8] Until that changes, Scorta should be valued as a differentiated early-stage product thesis with a compelling readiness wedge, not as a proven full transaction-rail company.

Scorta has the clearest no-login diagnostic and action log. Eilla publishes a compelling funnel but less evidence of a self-serve seller interface. None of the three publicly demonstrates an auditable lender handoff, a live lender decision, or autonomous execution across external portals.

The map-changing adjacent benchmark is Baton. Baton markets a 10-week listing-to-LOI process, a claim of being 10 times more likely to close and typical cost at half that of a traditional broker. content.8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligen:
The most defensible white space is a **sale-readiness operating layer for sub-USD 2M businesses** that does four things together: recasts financials deterministically, measures owner dependency and concentration risk, creates lender-ready evidence, and maintains a continuously updated sellability score. Scorta is closest in public thesis because its readiness dimensions, 90-day fix list, SBA pre-screen and staged lender-review package are explicit. [8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[0]] [8][8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[1]] [9] But no public evidence proves its internal ingestion stack or lender-portal work. The opportunity is therefore not to repeat the claim; it is to prove the handoff.

Eilla owns the strongest **high-value sell-side execution** position. The CreateX/Native Digital transaction and its 15-day offer claim show that its data-led buyer search can be attached to an actual advisory process. [8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[2]] [3][8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[3]] [2] Its challenge is economic and segmental: a roughly 5% fee on EUR 10M to EUR 20M deals does not automatically translate into an efficient sub-USD 2M model. [8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[3]] [2] A competitor could attack below Eilla by productizing the preparation that Eilla currently performs inside an advisory mandate.

Bizbe owns the strongest **trust and transaction-room UX** in public copy. Its proof-of-funds gate, KYC, private listings and live room make the buyer journey concrete. [8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[4]] [5] It also has the clearest current seller price, at 6.99%, once the onboarding package is included. [8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[5]] [20] Its open questions are operating rather than conceptual: how many of the six visible opportunities close, whether the FedEx specialization produces repeatable sourcing, and whether home-services inventory is material. [8_decision_ready_white_space_and_diligence_priorities[6]] [16]

For a competitor or investor, the next evidence request should be narrowly operational:

1. **Eilla**: request a dated mandate table showing deal size, sector, geography, signed NDA count, offers, close status and fee for every mandate after April 2026; request the sub-EUR/USD 5M fee card and one US or home-services reference.
2. **Bizbe**: request the legal entity's state licensing matrix, anonymized closed-deal count, seller onboarding invoices, the six-listing category mix, proof for the USD 10M-plus FedEx claim and the exact conditions for buyer representation fees.
3. **Scorta**: request a live lender handoff, a named SBA lender or written lender workflow, anonymized pre/post readiness scores, a customer-approved closing reference, and evidence that QBO/Gusto/Stripe/POS ingestion and continuous rescore are deployed rather than planned.

These requests test the mechanisms that matter. They do not reward generic AI claims, database size or polished demos unless those assets change time-to-close, lender approval, buyer conversion or realized fees.

Across five dimensions, the companies occupy distinct positions:

| Dimension | Eilla | Bizbe | Scorta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Human-led advisory augmented by buyer intelligence, CIM automation and data-room support. [synthesis[0]] [22] | Broker-led marketplace and transaction room with valuation, qualified access, diligence and close. [synthesis[1]] [5] | Readiness-first product intended to make the business financeable and saleable before matching. [synthesis[2]] [8][synthesis[3]] [9] |
| Scope and time horizon | Larger, cross-border, higher-value sell-side mandates; proof is strongest in one completed 2026 transaction. [synthesis[4]] [3][synthesis[5]] [2] | Immediate Main Street transaction flow; public inventory and fee disclosures are current, but close throughput is unclear. [synthesis[6]] [16][synthesis[7]] [20] | Early-stage infrastructure thesis; public roadmap and product UX reach beyond the current independent proof base. [synthesis[3]] [9] |
| Economics | Success fee only, about 5% on EUR 10M to EUR 20M average deals. [synthesis[5]] [2] | USD 2,500 onboarding plus 6.99% seller success fee; optional buyer representation at USD 1,500/month. [synthesis[7]] [20] | Free diagnostic and approximately 3% advertised flat success fee; actual realized economics unverified. [synthesis[3]] [9] |
| Evidence base | Best public deal evidence and funding corroboration. [synthesis[8]] [29][synthesis[4]] [3] | Best public legal pricing and access-control evidence, but funding and close claims remain open. [synthesis[7]] [20][synthesis[9]] [33] | Best readiness articulation, weakest independent proof of capitalization, integrations and closings. [synthesis[2]] [8][synthesis[9]] [33] |
| Trade-off | Strong credibility and data, but unclear low-ticket and home-services fit. | Concrete workflow and trust gates, but possible inventory and licensing constraints. | Potentially largest structural wedge, but execution and lender proof are missing. |

The non-obvious tension is that the most ambitious company, Scorta, has the least public proof, while the most proven company, Eilla, is economically furthest from the low-end Main Street problem. Bizbe sits between them: it has the most tangible public transaction interface and current fee disclosures, but its public positioning overstates certainty unless its legal terms, buyer fees, licensing and claimed FedEx volume are reconciled.

The practical conclusion is not that one company wins every category. Eilla is the benchmark for AI-assisted sell-side execution and disclosed deal proof. Bizbe is the benchmark for a transparent, qualified-buyer brokerage workflow. Scorta is the benchmark for sale-readiness as a product. The defensible unclaimed territory is the combination: a continuously sellable Main Street business record, lender-integrated SBA execution, transparent buyer access, and verified close outcomes at sub-USD 2M deal sizes.
